subject: Bivariate Gaussian hierarchical model keeps failing

messages.author: 6a368dde230699dd
messages.subject: Bivariate Gaussian hierarchical model keeps failing
parts:
I've got the latest version of rstan and just removed then reinstalled. gcc is version 4.8.4

I want to do several analyses just like 8-schools, but the response is bivariate. The model appears to run fine most of the time and the output seems sensible, but occasionally a chain appears to go into an infinite loop - one of my cores is running at 100%, but no additional output appears.

My first guess is that my model is wrongly specified, though I don't see where. I've tried various values for B, diag(1), diag(10^4), diag(2 * apply(x, 2, var)). W is diag(1).

I'd be grateful of any help.

Thanks,
Harry

data {
  int<lower=1> K; // Number of response variables
  int<lower=0> N; // Sample size
  vector[K] y[N]; // Response
  cov_matrix[K] S[N]; // Observed covariances corresponding to y

  vector[K] m; // Prior mean for mu
  cov_matrix[K] B; // Prior variance for mu
  cov_matrix[K] W; // Prior for Sigma
}
parameters {
  vector[K] mu; // Top level mean
  cov_matrix[K] Sigma;

  vector[K] theta[N]; // Deviations from top level mean (study effects)
}
model {
  mu ~ multi_normal(m, B);
  Sigma ~ inv_wishart(2, W);

  theta ~ multi_normal(mu, Sigma);

  for (i in 1:N)
    y[i] ~ multi_normal(theta[i], S[i]);
}

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Bivariate Gaussian hierarchical model keeps failing
parts:
We strongly recommend using Cholesky factors to parameterize
covariance. But we don't have the Wishart for that, only
the LKJ prior for correlation matrices, which we then scale.

The only advantage of Wisharts is that they're conjugate, which
doesn't matter for Stan. Speaking of which, can the following
block be simplified given that m and B and W are data and W is a unit
matrix.

> mu ~ multi_normal(m, B);
> Sigma ~ inv_wishart(2, W);
> theta ~ multi_normal(mu, Sigma);

There's a discussion of multivariate reparameterizations
starting on p. 218 of the Stan 2.9.0 manual.

- Bob

messages.author: 6a368dde230699dd
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Bivariate Gaussian hierarchical model keeps failing
parts:
Thanks for your response.

I've discovered a bug in how I was constructing my data (dividing by N then computing variance matrix, rather than the other way around - the amount of time a single misplaced bracket can cause). A slightly modified version of the code I originally posted is now running just fine and my chains are behaving nicely. I'll attempt to improve the code along the lines you suggest at some point, though.

Thanks again,
Harry
